To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a) the developed model of the 400/220 kV transmission substation with the protection system is suitable for the generation of synthetic data for knowledge extraction studies, and b) the knowledge extracted from the data base of the operating response of the relays and circuit breakers can be used for the development of a protection system expert system.

the proposed method is capable to extract the operating responses of each protection and relay and the associated breaker in a transmission substa- tion, and the operating responses can be used to extract knowledge for protection and control system design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a computer model of a transmission substation and the generation of a data base of fault records for use in knowledge extraction studies.
developing a methodology for knowledge extraction from the operating response of a protection and control system in power substations, which can be used in the future for fault diagnosis purposes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed methodology is a very powerful technique for knowledge extraction in power system protection.
the model developed in this thesis is a very useful tool for the study of power systems and the associated protection and control systems.
the proposed model is an accurate and reliable tool for the study of power systems and protection relays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an event data base for a substation with the complete protection and control system, using a simulation model developed using MATLAB and SimPowerSystems.

we are able to model the substation protection system, simulate the operating response for different fault scenarios, store the results in an event database and extract the knowledge for different protection schemes.
the models developed for the transmission substation and the protection system are very accurate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the model can be used to generate a huge amount of data, which can be used for training machine learning models to predict the operating state of the protection relaying system.
the models for the substation can be used as a test bench for testing and evaluating protection algorithms.
the models developed are very useful in the development of a data base for the training and testing of artificial intelligence (AI) techniques for fault classification.
